subject: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs

Team,

Before we enable Dedicated staged rollouts for any customer tenant (even “friendly” beta), we need to treat this as an operational-risk launch, not a feature toggle.

Requirements for go/no-go (non-negotiable):

1) SRE sign-off in writing
- I need a clear, explicit sign-off from the SRE owner for Dedicated pools that they’ve reviewed the gate evaluator failure modes + alerting + oncall runbooks.
- If we can’t get SRE sign-off, we do not enable for customer tenants.

2) Launch checklist + owner per line item
- Single checklist doc that includes: migrations, feature flags, dashboards/alerts, rollback plan, oncall readiness, support escalation path, and customer comms.
- Each item has an owner and a “done” criterion.

3) Guardrails must default to safe
- If metrics are missing/late, the rollout must HOLD (not advance).
- If evaluator is degraded, rollout advancement must STOP-THE-LINE.
- Any stage traffic weight changes must be deterministic and tenant-isolated.
- Dedicated pool headroom policy needs to be enforced (no stage-induced saturation).

4) Limited blast radius
- Start with internal dogfood pools only.
- Then max 2 pilot customers via explicit allowlist, not self-serve.

Please reply with (a) checklist link, (b) who is responsible for SRE sign-off, and (c) target date for readiness review.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
VP, Product & Platform
Redwood Inference


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs

Agree on all points.

(a) Checklist link (draft):
- “Dedicated staged rollouts launch checklist” (Drive) — Connor and I started this last week; it’s missing the SRE + Security sections right now.

(b) SRE sign-off owner:
- Proposing Rafa for formal sign-off (and Sean as reviewer). I’ll coordinate with Rachel on scheduling.

(c) Target readiness review:
- End of next week (Fri) if we can keep scope to: stage weights + default gates + hold/rollback + audit events + core dashboards.

Also: we should agree on a policy that “beta” still requires the same operational bar; we just narrow the blast radius.

Marissa

Redwood Inference


From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:21 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs

+1.

From the architecture side, I want to make sure the checklist calls out two additional operational risks that we’ve already seen in staging:

- State transitions under partial failure: approvals arriving concurrently with evaluator ticks, and “stuck between stages” behavior. We have a fix in flight, but I’d like this explicitly validated as part of readiness.

- Metrics freshness and evaluator lag: our gating logic is “pause on missing metrics,” but we need to define “missing” vs “late” thresholds and alert on evaluator lag. Otherwise we get silent slow-advancement or (worse) delayed holds.

Proposed checklist items (eng-owned):
1) Evaluator health SLO + alert (lag, success rate).
2) Gate query latency budget + explicit “data stale” behavior surfaced in status.
3) Control plane migrations: forward/backward compatible schema + rollback plan.

If helpful I can add a short “Failure modes / expected system behavior” appendix to the checklist so SRE has a crisp artifact to sign.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
Platform Architecture
Redwood Inference


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:07 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs

Adding security/compliance requirements to the checklist (these have come up repeatedly in enterprise reviews):

- Audit logging coverage: create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold events must be emitted, include actor identity + tenant + pool_id + plan version + stage id.
- RBAC enforcement: explicitly verify approve/abort/edit permissions. No “operator bypass” for enterprise tenants unless it’s a documented break-glass flow.
- Retention + export: confirm events flow to the existing audit export pipeline (and that we can answer “who approved what and when” for the pilot customers).

Also suggest we include a single paragraph of customer-facing language for “change management / approvals / audit trail” so CS isn’t inventing wording during beta.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:36 AM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs

Good. A few clarifications so we’re aligned:

- “SRE sign-off” means: an explicit reply in this thread stating the readiness criteria were reviewed and met (runbooks + alerts + failure modes), plus named oncall ownership for the beta period.

- The checklist needs to contain a hard “kill switch” plan (what to flip, where, how long it takes, and how we validate it actually stopped stage advancement + traffic shifting). I don’t want a theoretical rollback.

- Pilot scope: max 2 customer tenants, allowlisted, and we do not expand the allowlist until after the first pilot completes and we do a retro (even if informal).

Rachel: please ensure Support escalation path is on the checklist and that the pilot customers know what “pause” vs “rollback” will look like from their perspective.

If we can get the checklist to a “ready for review” state by EOD Thu, I’ll make time Fri afternoon for a go/no-go review.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
VP, Product & Platform
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 5:41 PM PT
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: launch guardrails & required sign-offs

Adding Dedicated-specific guardrails we should explicitly call out in the checklist (these are the things that can violate our SLA fastest):

1) Headroom policy during partial rollout
- For reserved pools, a 5%/25% stage still competes for shared queue + GPU time within the pool. We should enforce minimum headroom at the pool level before increasing stage weight.
- If headroom is below threshold (queue depth / utilization), hold stage advancement even if latency/error gates are “green.”

2) No cross-tenant interference
- Confirm routing changes are scoped by tenant + pool_id and cannot affect other Dedicated tenants on the same fleet.

3) Customer comms (beta)
- Rachel and I will draft a short FAQ explaining: what stage weights mean, what “hold” means, and what signals we watch (latency, 5xx, timeouts, queue depth, utilization).

I’ll add these items to the checklist draft tonight.

Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference
